pairs.difference: A (scarf): a soft key from the upper left, darker fold shadows on the right-hand tails and a gentle shadow inside the collar. It is low contrast but the light has a clear direction. B (lasso): the coil and loop are lit almost evenly from the front, with no real shadow side on the rope. The only darkening is a small core under the coil, and the rope barely casts a shadow onto the purple ground.
pairs.fix: Light the lasso from the upper left so the right and bottom side of each rope coil falls into a clear darker shadow, and put a soft contact shadow on the ground under the coil and the loop.

pairs.difference: A (boot): the shaft has a long glossy streak along its left edge, and the shadow side on the right stays shallow and orange. There is almost no shadow under the heel or the sole. B (grad cap): the top board has a lit face and a darker front edge, the band under it falls into deep shadow, and the tassel catches a small highlight. The form turns the way it does on the real cards.
pairs.fix: Make the boot leather matte with only a small soft sheen. Darken its right side and the inside of the shaft opening, and add a soft dark contact shadow under the heel and sole.

pairs.difference: A is the real computer from the lessons: a side key with a cool shadow side on the monitor's right and a deep shadow under the keyboard. B (saddle): lit straight from the front. The seat and flap shade the same on both sides, and the only darkening is a thin edge around the outline. The rail and stirrups throw no cast shadow (light bias 0.054, below the real range).
pairs.fix: Light the saddle from the upper left. Leave the right flap and the underside of the seat in a clear darker shadow, and have the saddle cast a shadow onto the wooden rail.

pairs.difference: A (book): a warm key from the upper left lights the pages, the page block has a darker front edge, and the cover has a contact shadow on the table. B (map): the sheets are lit flat and evenly. The lens shows a washed-out wash with weak directional shading, and only the stacked sheets have thin, faint shadows (shading range 0.62, light bias 0.155, both low).
pairs.fix: Light the map sheets from one side so the top sheet is brighter than the ones below. Put a darker soft shadow under each folded edge and onto the background.

pairs.difference: A (chest): strong top-left light on the gold lid, a deep shadow inside the open chest and under the lid, and a contact shadow in the sand. B (barrel): lit from the front and symmetrical. Both edges darken equally like a cylinder in a flat studio, the top lid is nearly flat, and a soft cast shadow drifts off to the right (shading range 0.639, low).
pairs.fix: Light the barrel from the upper left so the left staves are bright and the right third falls into a clearly darker shadow. Put a dark contact shadow where the barrel meets the floor.

pairs.difference: A (train): the boiler and cab are lit fairly evenly from the front, and the side panels are flat mid-grey with little turn into shadow. The light bias is weak and the shadows under the wheels are faint. B (coaster): the cars have a lit top and a darker underside, and the track loop has clear shading on its inner side.
pairs.fix: Give the locomotive a strong side light: bright on the top and front of the boiler, a darker shadow down its far side and under the running board, and a dark shadow on the ties beneath the wheels.

pairs.difference: A (popcorn cart): the awning has a lit top and shadowed scallops, the shadow inside the cart is deep, and the wheels sit on dark contact shadows. B (cactus): each arm and the trunk are shaded like a symmetrical cylinder, with equal dark bands on both edges and a lit centre, as if lit straight from the front. The rock and base contact shadows are weak (form contrast 0.39, low).
pairs.fix: Light the cactus from the upper left so the right side of the trunk and arms falls into a deeper green shadow. Add a soft dark shadow where the trunk enters the sand.

pairs.difference: A (saloon doors): the posts, beam and door panels are almost evenly lit, with barely any difference between the front faces and the side faces. The shadow on the floor is faint (form contrast 0.301 and light bias 0.068, both below the real range). B (sneakers): a clear key from the upper right, dark shadow sides on the soles, and a strong cast shadow to the left.
pairs.fix: Light the saloon doors from the upper left. Make the post side faces and the underside of the top beam clearly darker than the front faces, and add a soft shadow on the floor under the doors and at the post feet.

pairs.difference: A (medal box): a top-left key, a deep shadow inside the lid, and a lit rim on the coin. B (sheriff star): the star is lit straight from the front, and each point is split into light and dark halves along a centre ridge in the same way all round. The ball tips have the same highlight, with no clear shadow side and no shadow onto the background.
pairs.fix: Light the star from the upper left so the points on the lower right fall into darker shadow. Give the ball tips one small highlight each, facing the same light.

pairs.difference: A (boat): a soft top light, a deep shadow inside the hull, and a contact shadow on the water. B (wagon): the canvas cover is lit almost evenly, and the wheel and tongue cast a hard, sharp shadow onto the road. The strong one-sided bias (0.905, above the real range) comes from that cast shadow, not from the wagon's form turning.
pairs.fix: Soften the wagon's cast shadow and keep it close under the wheels. Shade the canvas cover so its far side and the inside of the opening are clearly darker.

pairs.difference: A (lion): soft top light on the mane and paws and darker sides on the plinth steps. The contrast is a bit low, but it is in keeping with the real cards. B (AC unit): the very high light bias comes from the painted cool airflow beams and light falling across the wall, not from how the unit itself is shaded. The unit has a lit top and a shadowed underside, which reads as consistent with the real cards. Neither card clearly breaks from the real cards on lighting.

A (scout jacket): a side key, deep shadows under the sash, in the pockets and inside the sleeves, and a clear shadow side on the right. B (cowboy hat): the crown is shaded evenly from the front, with a soft glow behind it and little shadow under the brim. The brim's underside and the band don't go dark, so the hat floats with no cast shadow.
pairs.fix: Light the hat from the upper left. Put a dark shadow under the brim across the band and on the right side of the crown, with a single soft highlight on the crown's lit side.

pattern: On the generated cards, light still hits the hero straight from the front and evenly. Their cylinders and stars shade the same on both sides, darkening at both edges instead of having one clear shadow side, so the shadow side stays shallow. Contact shadows are missing or faint, or the cards swap them for one hard cast shadow. Real cards use a single side key with a deep, cool shadow side, dark hollows, and solid contact shadows.
